title: From a chart to a message

steps.say: Thirteen coloured lines and a legend: an exploratory chart. Good for finding the story, hard for anyone else to read.
Grey for the context, one colour for the point. Every region stays on the chart, but the eye goes straight to Jazan.
Label the line where it ends, instead of a legend the reader has to decode.
Say the finding in the title, keep the units in the subtitle, and drop what does not help. The same data, now an argument.
Make the story checkable: up is computed from the data, and the highlight, the label and the title all use it. Next quarter the claim is tested, not assumed.

final:
---
title: "Unemployment by region"
format:
  html:
    embed-resources: true
execute:
  echo: false
---

```{r}
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
rates <- read_csv("unemployment.csv") |>
  filter(region != "Kingdom")
up <- rates |>
  group_by(region) |>
  summarise(change = last(rate) - first(rate)) |>
  filter(change > 0) |>
  pull(region)
up_end <- rates |>
  filter(region %in% up) |>
  slice_tail(n = 1)
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.5
ggplot(rates, aes(date, rate, group = region)) +
  geom_line(colour = "grey80") +
  geom_line(data = filter(rates, region %in% up),
            colour = "#00803A", linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_text(data = up_end, aes(label = region),
            hjust = -0.15, colour = "#00803A") +
  scale_x_date(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.12))) +
  labs(title = str_glue("{up} rose while every other region fell"),
       subtitle = "Unemployment rate, %, 2022 Q1 to 2025 Q4",
       x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
```
